title: Sorrify-at-failure: five common sorry types and their responses
intent: Classify why a sorry resists filling into five ordered types so the filler picks the right response: search/tactic/have for the cheap cases, and for the structural case (Type 4) replace the too-large goal with sub-sorries and work them one at a time, escalating to a separate helper lemma (Type 5) when the hole is a missing statement.

applicability.goal_shape: A Lean goal sitting under a `sorry` (or hole) that resists direct filling: it is a missed library search (Type 1), needs the right tactic (Type 2), misses a connecting `have` fact (Type 3), is structurally too large (Type 4), or is in fact a missing lemma (Type 5).
applicability.use_when: a hole has resisted 2-3 direct candidates and you must choose between searching, a tactic, a `have`, a sub-sorry split, or a helper lemma; use the sub-sorry split (Type 4) only when the proof is structurally complex but does not need a new fact.
applicability.avoid_when: the hole is only a missed search (search first), a routine goal (try the tactic), or a missing statement (extract a lemma, do not sorrify); the section orders these so the structural split is last-resort and itself marked 'rare'.

claims.claim: The section 'Common Sorry Types' (lines 88-103) classifies why a sorry resists filling into exactly five types, each heading stating a frequency in order: 'most common' (Type 1), 'common' (Type 2), 'less common' (Type 3), 'rare' (Type 4), 'very rare' (Type 5).

Type 4's prescribed response is the sorrify-at-failure move verbatim: 'Break into sub-sorries with clear strategy' (lines 99-100), i.e. replace the too-large goal with several holes and work them one at a time.

For the very rare case the authors name a missing statement and prescribe extracting it to a separate lemma: 'Actually needs new lemma (very rare)' with 'Extract as helper lemma, prove separately' (lines 102-103).
The same two structural responses recur as the first two escalation options in 'When to Escalate': 'Break into smaller sub-sorries' and 'Extract as helper lemma' (lines 251-253).

metrics.how_counted: counted the five `### Type N` headings in lines 88-103 of the copied file; Types 4 and 5 are the two structural responses (sub-sorries, helper lemma)

consequences: Sorrifying a structural goal (Type 4) creates several smaller holes, each still needing a filler and its own verification gate (`lake env lean`); it shrinks each obligation but not the total. Extracting a helper lemma (Type 5) introduces a new top-level statement that must be stated faithfully (its hypotheses and universals) and proved, with the original hole becoming an application of it. Both are marked 'rare'/'very rare', so over-applying them where a search or a tactic would close the goal is the failure mode.
